brief.headline: Weekend check: aluminium holds Friday's bounce to $3,012 three-month - still $58 lower on the week and below the July low - with no new LME session until Monday, while fresh Hormuz mine-strike reports keep energy-cost risk elevated.
bullets: WHERE IT STANDS: the board is Friday's 16-October LME official - cash $3,014.00 (+$15.00), three-month $3,012.00 (+$17.50, +0.58%), a $2.00 backwardation (cash above three-month) and LME stock at a new low of 237,875 t. Nothing trades on the LME until Monday's 13:20 London official.

WEEKEND NEWS: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that two crude tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz (reported via Reuters, not independently confirmed), after attacks in the area increased over the past two weeks. That adds to Friday's jump in Brent (~$110) and European gas (~EUR 88/MWh, highest since December 2022) - a higher energy-cost floor for smelters outside China.

THE BEARISH SIDE IS UNCHANGED: ex-China physical demand is weak (SMM, 16-October: offers falling in South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam, a stagnant US market), Gulf restarts are progressing, and markets still price a December Fed hike.

WHAT TO WATCH THIS WEEK: Monday's open after the Hormuz reports; whether three-month settles back above $3,061.5-3,077 (decline ending) or below about $2,977.5 (new leg lower); China's September output data from the statistics bureau (expected around 19-20 October); the October carbon-input settlements; the 27-28 October FOMC.

lme.commentary: A FRIDAY BOUNCE, BUT A WEEK OF DAMAGE. On the Friday 16-October official cash settled $3,014.00, up $15.00, and three-month $3,012.00, up $17.50 or 0.58% - back $1.50 above the 02-January three-month official, but still $49.50 beneath the 3,061.5 July low and down $58.00 on the week. The backwardation narrowed to $2.00 from $4.50 - spread and price moved in opposite directions for a second session - and visible stock slipped 250 t to a new series low of 237,875 t. The whole complex rose (nickel +1.5%, copper +0.9%) as the dollar index fell about 0.75% to near 101.8, its first weekly decline in four weeks (Trading Economics). Trading Economics continues to frame October's slide as the war premium being erased by faster Gulf restarts, Bell Bay's extension and surging Chinese alloy exports. SMM (16-October) describes ex-China physical markets as weak, with offers under pressure in Korea, Thailand and Vietnam and a stagnant US market. September's official means were cash $3,276.82 and three-month $3,272.89.

drivers.text: The Q4 Japanese premium has settled 35% lower, at $255/t — SETTLED: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed to pay $255/t over LME cash for October-December shipments, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below producers' initial offers of $310-325/t; producers named in the talks included Rio Tinto and South32, and talks with other buyers were ongoing. A Japanese trading-house source cited recovering Middle East output after the March attacks on Gulf smelters and rising Indonesian shipments. Negotiations ran longer than usual because of a wide gap between the two sides. The settlement sits inside the $245-260/t offer range AL Circle reported on 06-October, and above CRU's $202/t Asia CIF assessment. WHY IT MATTERS: the quarterly MJP is the reference for much Asian physical business, so the regional premium level resets about $140/t lower for the quarter.
drivers.source: Reuters via LSE.co.uk - Some Japanese aluminium buyers agree to pay Q4 premiums of $255/t, 35% lower than Q3 (07-Oct-2026)

drivers.text: Spot premiums have fallen below the new quarterly benchmark - but sellers' pressure is easing — SMM's 09-October assessment puts CIF Japan MJP spot at $230/t, $25 beneath the $255/t Q4 quarterly settlement, with Korea at $216-223/t and Thailand at $249/t. SMM concludes the outlook for overseas premiums 'has become less bearish' and premiums may stabilise or recover modestly near term, but a stronger rebound needs clearer improvement in downstream orders and restocking. WHY IT MATTERS: with spot below the quarterly benchmark, remaining Japanese buyers have little reason to settle above $255/t, and the Q1-2027 talks start from a lower spot base.
drivers.source: SMM - Overseas primary aluminum premiums near a floor as selling pressure eases (09-Oct-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese primary imports fell 14.65% year on year in August, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China metal — Public customs data reported on 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports at 185,500 tonnes, DOWN 14.65% year on year and up just 0.16% month on month, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia (2,920 t), Indonesia (2,180 t) and Malaysia (1,800 t) accounting for almost all of the remainder. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED: domestic capacity is at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient, and inventory is being drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR PREMIUMS EVEN SO: a premium is set by competition for units at a location. China importing 14.65% less primary metal, and 96% of what it does import arriving from a single discounted-origin supplier, means the marginal ex-China unit faces less Chinese competition - which works against premiums in Japan, Europe and the United States regardless of why Chinese buying fell.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China Aug aluminium imports down 14.7% year on year, Russia accounts for 96% of supply (25-September-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese semis exports hit a 2026 high, which pressures converter margins in exactly the markets where premiums are assessed — Public data reported on 25-September show China's August aluminium extrusion exports at 92,500 tonnes, the highest monthly figure of 2026, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 tonnes and 3.0% month on month from 89,800 tonnes, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; the share of processing trade rose while ordinary trade fell, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE PREMIUM READ IS SPECIFIC: extrusions compete with locally converted metal in third markets. More Chinese semis arriving in South-East Asia, Africa and Latin America pressures the converter margins that ultimately support regional ingot premiums, even though the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China's August aluminium extrusion exports hit a YTD high; pullback expected in September amid narrowing price spread (25-September-2026)

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: REVIEWED SATURDAY 10-OCTOBER-2026. Trading Economics' Brent coverage (09-October) says the US-Iran conflict continues to strain shipping: tankers are tied up in ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, freight rates are at record highs and eleven tankers were attacked in the Strait in the week ending 04-October; President Trump said the US would not strike Iran again before the midterm elections. No container or bulk transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP pending a public, verifiable normalisation signal. PRIOR: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 30-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 29-September records the US rejecting Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, new US sanctions on 10 suppliers to Iran's military, and Tehran awaiting a formal US response to its ceasefire proposal; the Strait remains closed. Middle East crude exports reached 12.8 million b/d, the highest since February, but largely via ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline bypasses that do not serve Gulf aluminium exports. No transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP. PRIOR: REVIEWED TUESDAY 29-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 28-September records indirect US-Iran talks resuming through mediators in New York, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed to commercial shipping; Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumed after drone-strike repairs, with flows reported near 3.5 million b/d, offering a partial bypass for crude but not for Gulf aluminium exports. Transit counts remain disputed between trackers and outlets, so no transit figure is published. Arrow stays UP until a dated, verifiable reopening step. PRIOR: REVIEWED MONDAY 28-SEPTEMBER-2026. On Saturday 26-September the US President publicly rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap - release of frozen funds, lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the naval blockade within four to five days, with the Strait reopened and negotiations under way by day seven - calling it not acceptable. He told reporters he expects talks to resume in the coming week; separately, US officials were reported as signalling a renewed bombing campaign after the November midterms. Iran's foreign minister said Tehran will not back down on its conditions and awaits mediators' formal feedback. Public tracking (straits.live, 27-September) classifies the Strait as closed to commercial traffic on day 210, with a pre-crisis baseline of about 85 transits a day; some outlets report sizeable US-escorted crude movements, so transit counts are DISPUTED and none is used as a figure here. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW GOES FROM FLAT BACK TO UP: last week's cut to flat rested on a visible negotiation; its latest proposal was publicly rejected and a post-midterm escalation path was reported. Second-order effects stand: regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices freight on lanes that never touch the Strait.

No public transit count newer than the prior reading was located, so none is published. Arrow stays UP. PRIOR: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 23-SEPTEMBER-2026. SMM's 23-September summary records that on 22-September US President Trump, speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated that the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERM ELECTIONS; that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York and Trump described a three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation as very productive with another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. READ THIS CAREFULLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY. A negotiation is now visibly under way, which is the first genuine de-escalation signal of this cycle. But the publicly stated US timetable puts any agreement AFTER November, and Iran's stated conditions are maximalist. The transit constraint is therefore still in force today and is not publicly guided to clear inside this quarter. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT AS SETTLED OUTCOMES.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 35.2% directional hit rate against a 67.3% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 0.74% versus 6.81% after 'loosening' readings. backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (108 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-07-17). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

The quarterly split is the material part - Q2-2026 revenue RMB 60.61bn, DOWN 1.9% y/y, and Q2 attributable net profit RMB 3.53bn, DOWN 26.2% y/y, against a Q1 that had risen 56.35%. THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA PRODUCER EARNED MATERIALLY LESS IN A QUARTER WHEN THE LME CASH AVERAGE WAS ABOVE $3,200, AND THAT IS THE SIGNAL. A 26% year-on-year fall in Q2 attributable profit on flat-to-lower revenue points to margin compression rather than volume weakness, and it is consistent with the Chinese alumina spot picture carried on this board - SMM's Shandong index down toward 2,600 RMB/t with national capacity utilisation rising and trader inventories building. For a reader of the seaborne market the implication runs both ways: weaker Chinese alumina margins are disinflationary for the smelter cost basket globally, but a large integrated producer earning less at a high metal price also argues that the cost curve has moved up underneath everyone. The shares fell around 3% on the release. NOTE: the reported H1 attributable profit of RMB 7.071bn does not reconcile with the sum of the reported Q1 and Q2 quarterly figures, and that discrepancy is disclosed on the earnings-history panel rather than resolved by inference.

earnings.note: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both drivers reverse by design once the holiday ends: stockpiled metal is consumed rather than bought, and the spread normalises. If Chinese inventory rebuilds sharply in the first two weeks of October, the single strongest bullish number on this page will have been a calendar effect; if it does not rebuild, the destock was demand and the deficit case strengthens materially.
